summary: Enum-driven conditional field setter. Dispatches on a2 through the jump table at 0x005542B0, maps one of the accepted enum values (1,2,3,4,5,6,13,14) to a dword field of `this`, and stores a3 there when the selected pointer is non-null and the current value differs. Returns 1 when a write occurred, 0 when the enum is invalid or the field already held a3.

local_names.a2: enum selector selecting which dword field of `this` to write
local_names.a3: incoming value stored into the selected field
local_names.v3: pointer to the field selected by the enum case

operations.description: Dispatch on enum value a2 through the jump table at 0x005542B0; cases 1,2,3,4,5,6,13,14 select a field pointer, any other value falls through to the default path that returns 0.
Map enum a2 to a dword field of `this`: 1->this+0x00, 2->this+0x04, 3->this+0x08, 4->this+0x14, 5->this+0x18, 6->this+0x1C, 13->this+0x0C, 14->this+0x10.
Skip the write when the selected field pointer is null or the current field value already equals a3 (*v3 == a3).
For enum value 14 the target is this+4 (byte offset 0x10): store a3 into this+0x10 when the current value differs.
Write the incoming value: *v3 = a3 into the selected field, and set result to 1.
Return 1 when a field was changed, 0 when the enum was invalid or the field already held a3.

unresolved: The class behind `this` and the semantics of each mapped dword field are unidentified.

Packet existing-analysis prose claims enum 5 maps to this[4]; the raw source maps case 5 to this+6 (offset 0x18), so the attested 0x10 field is written by case 14, not case 5. Raw source wins over the prose mapping.
